title: Non-profit or social enterprise
tagline: A mission-first organisation — Section 8 company, trust or society — that may still sell products or services.
who: Founders building education, health, livelihood or climate programmes
Teams that want grants and CSR funding
Social businesses weighing non-profit vs for-profit structures

structure.recommended: Section 8 company (non-profit company under the Companies Act)
structure.why: CSR donors and foundations strongly prefer Section 8 companies: MCA governance, audited accounts, no dividends, eligibility for 12A/80G income-tax registrations and, after three years, FCRA for foreign grants. Trusts and societies are cheaper but state-regulated and less trusted by institutional donors. A revenue-generating social business can run a for-profit private limited alongside.
structure.alternatives: Public charitable trust (state Registrar) or society (Societies Registration Act) for small, local, grant-funded work; private limited for a social business that pays founders and raises impact investment.

breakdown: Section 8 incorporation (SPICe+ with INC-12 licence): ₹10,000–30,000 professional fee; MCA fee waived for Section 8
CSR-1 registration on MCA to receive CSR funds: free

timeline: Section 8 licence and incorporation 3–5 weeks; 12A/80G provisional registration 1–3 months; FCRA only after three years of activity.
taxes: Income exempt under sections 11/12 (now re-numbered in the 2025 Act) once registered under 12A; donors get 50% deduction with your 80G certificate (Form 10BE must be issued to donors and 10BD filed annually).
GST applies to any commercial supply — training fees, product sales — above ₹20 lakh; pure grants and donations without quid pro quo are outside GST.
TDS on salaries, consultants and rent as any employer; Section 8 companies file ITR-7 by 31 October with Form 10B/10BB audit.
Accumulate at most 15% of income; apply 85% to objects each year or file Form 10 to accumulate for up to five years.
selling: CSR partnerships (register in CSR-1; comply with the company’s CSR policy and reporting)
Grants: foundations, government schemes, GuideStar/NGO Darpan listings
Earned income: training, products made by beneficiaries (keep GST and labelling compliant like any seller)
sourcing: Volunteers and fellows — written agreements, stipends through payroll with TDS where applicable
pitfalls: Paying founders ‘honorarium’ in cash without TDS or appointment resolutions — Section 8 companies can pay reasonable remuneration, but it must be approved and documented.
Taking foreign donations (including from NRIs’ foreign accounts) before FCRA registration — a criminal offence under FCRA.
Missing the 80G renewal cycle (registrations are now time-bound and renewed every five years) and Form 10BD donor statements.
Mixing programme and commercial income without separate books.
